description: Dated, evidence-linked frames for the public site and future research films. Source-derived counts; no private keys or derived addresses.

entries.title: Boundaries, tested.
entries.summary: Where the edge falls changes the word. Every allowed pair-local choice was included.
entries.result: All 222 shaped strings failed their checksums. This result covers the registered pair-local model.
entries.sceneNote: Illustrative page view. The evidence link contains the exact tested rule and scope.

entries.title: One weak checksum hit.
entries.summary: The search connected all four directed page pairs without choosing a convenient reading.
entries.result: A one-byte checksum can pass by chance. The next frame tests the lead against Bitcoin history.
entries.sceneNote: Illustrative page view. The evidence link contains the exact tested rule and scope.

entries.title: Five addresses. Zero history.
entries.summary: Two independent implementations derived the same five standard address constructions.
entries.result: Both providers reported zero chain and mempool history. Other wallet constructions and the puzzle remain open.
entries.sceneNote: Illustrative page view. The evidence link contains the exact tested rule and scope.

entries.title: A checker gap. One weak lead.
entries.summary: The old Orange Party readings were replayed through the missing format checks. Two implementations agreed.
entries.result: One 22-character minikey passed an eight-bit check. It is compatible with chance; history checking is next.
entries.sceneNote: Actual retained Orange Party scans. The 3D arrangement is a viewing aid; the evidence fixes the tested readings.

entries.title: Orange Party lead. Zero history.
entries.summary: The weak checksum lead was checked through five fixed constructions after independent address agreement.
entries.result: Both providers returned ten successful all-zero chain and mempool summaries. Other constructions and the puzzle remain open.
entries.sceneNote: Actual retained Orange Party scans. Viewing geometry does not reveal or authenticate a key.

entries.title: Twelve steps. No checksum pass.
entries.summary: The printed phrase motivated one fixed reading rule over the reviewed Orange Party body. Both implementations agreed.
entries.result: All 93 minikey-shaped strings failed. Sixty readings use confirmed glyphs; twelve retain prefix uncertainty. Other interpretations remain open.
entries.sceneNote: Actual retained Orange Party scans. The row/token convention and uncertain prefixes are fixed in the linked evidence.

entries.title: The missing length. One weak hit.
entries.summary: Historical software accepted 26-character mini keys. The same 42 forms and 24 mirror language graphs were checked.
entries.result: One of 207 shaped strings passed an eight-bit checksum. Independent replay agreed; source and history review remain open.
entries.sceneNote: Original Issue 24 scans. The page view illustrates the source; it does not disclose or authenticate the checksum lead. The protocol fixes both populations.

entries.title: Five addresses. Zero reported history.
entries.summary: The 26-character checksum lead was checked through five fixed constructions after exact Python/Node agreement.
entries.result: All ten provider responses reported zero chain and mempool statistics. This covers those constructions at check time; the puzzle remains open.
entries.sceneNote: Original Issue 24 source scans. The viewing arrangement is illustrative; private candidate and address associations are omitted. The linked protocol defines the checked scope.

entries.title: A source gap, made visible.
entries.summary: A retained Keiser column had only documented visual-control coverage. Its six article pages are now inspectable.
entries.result: Eight scans reviewed: six article pages and two separately labelled ads. Exact issue/date remain unverified. This is source preparation, with no new cipher test.
entries.sceneNote: Actual retained Funky Upheaval scans, printed107–112. The arrangement is a viewing aid. Issue/date and eligibility under the December claim remain unresolved; the photographed March target is still Issue24.

entries.title: Three readings. No clear second message.
entries.summary: First words, odd whole lines and the even-line control were generated from the frozen source. Both implementations agreed.
entries.result: Two AI contexts read all three complete outputs and recognized no clear second message. This is exploratory nonrecognition, not proof that a key or cipher is absent.
entries.sceneNote: Actual Funky Upheaval scans. The arrangement is a viewing aid; registered rules fix the readings. Issue/date remain unverified, and the March mirror/20BTC claim is not assigned to this column.

entries.title: The detector matches. Spacing stays open.
entries.summary: The registered diagnostic traced every lexical region using the original optical rule. All saved first-guard outcomes matched.
entries.result: The same 38 rows still fail measurement. No gaps, bits or decodes were generated; a source-support fixture comes next.
entries.sceneNote: Actual source pages; camera placement is illustrative. Native strips below show contrast changes and punctuation, not a decoded message.

entries.title: Two rows checked. A source limit exposed.
entries.summary: Every body row received a first contrast review. Independent pixel checks verified the atlas, and two pilot rows now have accepted token masks.
entries.result: Only 22 token masks are independently accepted. Inverse-field joins and edge residue stop full original-glyph certification. Spacing remains inconclusive; no new decode ran.
entries.sceneNote: Actual source scans open in 3D. The excerpts show accepted pilot memberships and remaining source uncertainty.

exhibits.label: Accepted pilot · separate words and dashes

entries.title: The opener gap is checked.
entries.summary: Two previously omitted opener lines joined the unchanged body and display units. Three fixed readings were generated after public registration.
entries.result: No valid declared-format record. Two AI contexts read every output without recognizing a coherent second message. This closes the small source correction; the puzzle remains unsolved.
entries.sceneNote: Actual opener and article scans. Pages 73–80 are now available in the 3D viewer. Display arrangement is illustrative; the registered source fixes the reading order.

entries.title: 40 orange-mask texts, read in full.
entries.summary: Two AI contexts read all 40 historical forward orange-mask texts, including eight from correct physical pairs and 32 other-pair controls.
entries.result: Neither reader recognized a determinate puzzle instruction. This is subjective nonrecognition with prior source exposure; no new cipher run or formal message exclusion.
entries.sceneNote: Actual source scans. The stack is a viewing aid; it does not apply the historical selector. The evidence separates physical-pair readings from other-pair controls.

entries.title: Extra formats. No valid record.
entries.summary: The registered compatibility replay covered seven frozen cohorts containing 2,594 saved readings. Both implementations agreed on all forms and validation results.
entries.result: All 186 cohort-level validations failed. Other added formats had no shapes. This closes the stated format gap on existing outputs; it does not exclude other readings or the puzzle.
entries.sceneNote: Actual source scans behind the historical outputs. This viewer illustrates the source; the replay used the frozen artifacts and did not rebuild geometry.

entries.title: Saved OCR. No valid extra record.
entries.summary: The same 1,038 saved spectral-OCR records produced 1,464 unchanged forms. Six address validations and two 26-character minikey checks all failed.
entries.result: The independent replay matched the complete records, forms and validation results. This closes the declared format gap on these saved outputs; OCR misses and other readings remain possible.
entries.sceneNote: Actual magazine scans behind the saved OCR. This viewer illustrates the source; the replay did not regenerate the 112 historical OCR views.

entries.title: Four paths. One weak checksum pass.
entries.summary: Four saved populations reproduced byte for byte: 43,699 correlated records and 5,557 forms summed across them. One 26-character minikey passed its eight-bit checksum in a whitespace-compacted Orange Party stride form.
entries.result: The independent replay matched every original artifact, form and validation record. The pass is in the source-known subset, but is not contiguous in an unmodified reading. A weak checksum can pass by chance; no recovered key or prize is authenticated.
entries.sceneNote: Actual Orange Party source pages. The check replays frozen readings; the page-board, layers and mirror are viewing aids. Choose another source set to inspect Censorship or Funky Upheaval.

entries.title: Five addresses. Zero history in scope.
entries.summary: Node and independent Python agreed on all five standard mainnet constructions. Both providers returned ten valid HTTP 200 responses with every chain and mempool statistic zero.
entries.result: The complete saved address vectors and provider receipts were independently checked. No funding evidence within these constructions at the recorded times. The weak checksum and other readings remain open; no prize is authenticated.
entries.sceneNote: Actual Orange Party body pages 80–81. The lead requires registered whitespace compaction; this is a viewing aid, not a displayed or authenticated printed key.

entries.title: 152 saved texts, read in full.
entries.summary: Two AI contexts report reading all saved alternating row texts for an intermediate instruction. Neither recognized one.
entries.result: Subjective nonrecognition in this fixed set. A's prior ledger exposure exceeded the plan; B reported a fresh context. No general exclusion.
entries.sceneNote: Original Issue 24 scans. The mirror illustrates the source; the review used saved texts and did not rerun extraction.

entries.title: The stencil boundary, mapped.
entries.summary: Both sides’ highlight colors were checked throughout each frozen word center’s guard square.
entries.result: Two implementations agree. All 97 uncertain words remain explicit alternatives in the fixed model. No reading or key check ran.
entries.sceneNote: Actual Issue 24 page 77. The mirror is an inspection aid; the report defines all four two-sided pairs.

entries.title: 152 languages had no declared format pattern.
entries.summary: All 160 registered stencil languages completed. Exhaustive flat checks agreed for 72 of them.
entries.result: Eight languages admitted WIF or minikey syntax. No hex64 or BIP39 pattern appeared in the registered model. The run stopped at syntax.
entries.sceneNote: Actual Issue 24 page 77 in mirror view. The registered model covers four directed page pairs and their combined scope.

entries.title: Five languages still admit a format pattern.
entries.summary: The shared-query model gives both directions on each leaf one common offset. Eight languages had admitted syntax in the prior model.
entries.result: Five still admit a declared pattern and three lose all declared patterns under this model. The test checked syntax only. Physical alignment was not measured.
entries.sceneNote: Actual Issue 24 page 77 in mirror view. The modeled offsets apply to leaves 76/77 and 78/79.

entries.title: Pages 78/79 show trim on both axes.
entries.summary: Two readers independently marked the same fixed sampling lines in the retained photographs.
entries.result: Both faces of 78/79 show agreed bottom and outer edges. Pages 76/77 show the bottom edge on both faces. Their outer edges remain unresolved. A separate calibration study is needed.
entries.sceneNote: The 3D viewer uses the higher-resolution page 78 scan. The guides below use the lower-resolution photographs tested here.

entries.title: One disputed crop shows an upside-down banknote.
entries.summary: Two readers compared the original ink and its reflection at the saved G07 locations.
entries.result: Neither reader recognized a reading instruction. A lossless turn clarified the one disputed banknote crop. The original disagreement remains in the review.
entries.sceneNote: The viewer opens the original Issue 24 opener. The paired examples and exact turned crop appear below.

entries.title: A faint title resembles the next page.
entries.summary: Two AI readers inspected all eight scanned pages. A faint mark on page 74 sent us back to the page 75 heading.
entries.result: Seventeen reports remain unclear. The heading resemblance is consistent with show-through. The comparison leaves physical alignment unmeasured.
entries.sceneNote: Explore the original page 74 scan in the mirror viewer. The source excerpts below use matching nominal coordinates and a horizontal flip of page 74.

entries.title: The trace is too faint to read.
entries.summary: Two readers marked the same faint band in the second scan. They recorded page 74 before seeing the page 75 heading.
entries.result: Neither reader could confidently read a word in the page 74 band. The match remains inconclusive.
entries.sceneNote: The 3D viewer opens page 74 in the higher-resolution scan. Both excerpts below come from the second retained scan.

entries.title: 142 lines align. One letter case stays open.
entries.summary: Two independent line inventories agree on the printed boundaries. The excerpts show the one damaged initial with conflicting case readings.
entries.result: No changed first or last word identity was found. The exact case of one initial remains open across the two source views.
entries.sceneNote: The viewer opens the higher-resolution page 77. The two excerpts show the same row in the retained source scans.

entries.title: The reflected trace matches in the sharper scan.
entries.summary: Match the upright heading against reflected page 74, then test the same shift on five held-out body regions.
entries.result: Four body regions pass in the sharper raster. The two lower-resolution heading offsets disagree.
entries.sceneNote: The 3D view opens the sharper scan of page 74. The excerpts show nominal crops. The report records the measured local shift.

entries.title: Page 74’s geometry falls short.
entries.summary: Use ordinary printed landmarks to predict how each face moves between scans.
entries.result: Page 75 passes. Page 74’s held-out errors and coverage leave the faint target unscored.
entries.sceneNote: The 3D viewer shows page 74 and its reflection. The excerpts show ordinary same-face landmarks from both scans.

exhibits.label: Same-face landmarks · sharp label and artwork
Additional landmarks and the upper print edge

entries.title: The sharper scan favors a lowercase initial.
entries.summary: Compare the surviving first-letter ink against known B and b on the same printed row.
entries.result: The sharper initial falls with the lowercase shape. The second scan’s controls leave its target unscored.
entries.sceneNote: The 3D view opens the sharper page 77 scan. The letter crops are exact native excerpts enlarged for inspection.

exhibits.label: Native sharper-scan initial and case controls
Ordinary and case control patches from both scans

entries.title: The archived clue leaves out a repeated line.
entries.summary: Check whether the archived first-word example’s excluded row has a counterpart in the printed sources.
entries.result: Issue 24 has a rewrapped editorial quotation and no matching first-eight color pattern. The Issue 26 literal comparison yielded no instruction.
entries.sceneNote: The viewer opens Issue 24 page 78. The separate Issue 26 excerpt shows the nine prose lines above STOP.

exhibits.label: Issue 26 · nine opener lines before the callout

entries.title: Right alignment repeats.
entries.summary: Compare the last four lines on page 78 with six nearby text blocks in both retained scans.
entries.result: The same right-alignment test passes on pages 77, 78 and 79. The page 78 margin alone gives no unique starting point.
entries.sceneNote: The viewer opens page 78. The chart below shows the measured edge positions for all three right-aligned blocks.

exhibits.label: Measured text spans on pages 77–79 in both scans

entries.title: Could the next word fit?
entries.summary: Compare the estimated endpoint of “to” against the visible ink of the next line in both scans.
entries.result: The estimate goes past the sharper scan’s visible line extent. The lower-resolution estimate overlaps it. The original frame width remains unknown.
entries.sceneNote: Open the printed page in the spread viewer. The chart shows measured bounds from both scans.

exhibits.label: Estimated endpoint of the next word versus visible ink in both scans
